name: Floating abdominoplasty

card.summary: A tummy-tuck variant in which the navel is detached from its stalk and repositioned so loose lower-abdominal skin can be removed through a smaller incision, flattening the stomach.
card.note: A surgical procedure with complication risks; performed by qualified plastic surgeons.

quick.overview:
Floating abdominoplasty is a form of tummy tuck, a body-contouring operation that removes excess lower-abdominal skin and fat and can tighten the muscle wall. In the floating version the navel is temporarily detached and then reattached or repositioned so that the skin can be pulled down and removed through a smaller incision.

People seek it for a flatter midsection and a trimmer waistline, for example after pregnancy or weight loss. It appears among surgical body procedures in looksmaxxing discussions of the torso.
quick.how: It is carried out in an operating room under anaesthesia by a plastic surgeon. The navel is freed from the abdominal wall, skin is lifted and excess removed, the muscle layer may be tightened and the navel is secured at its new position. Recovery involves dressings, possible drains and a compression garment.
quick.risks: Abdominoplasty overall is described as generally safe in qualified hands but with a higher complication rate than many cosmetic operations: fluid collection (seroma), bleeding, infection, wound-healing problems, scarring, altered sensation and blood clots. Smoking, obesity, diabetes and combined procedures raise the risk.

lead: Floating abdominoplasty, also called the umbilical float or FAB technique, is a variant of abdominoplasty (tummy tuck). The navel is released from the abdominal wall so that skin and fat below it can be removed and the navel brought down to a natural position, often within a mini-abdominoplasty with a limited incision.[1][2]

The appearance goal is a flatter, tighter lower abdomen with a lower, shorter scar than a full tummy tuck. Surgeons describe choosing the technique for patients with loose skin or muscle separation mainly below the navel, and some surgeons discuss it as a way of avoiding a scar around the navel or of keeping its position.[2][3]

Abdominoplasty belongs to the group of body-contouring procedures and is one of the most common aesthetic operations. A Czech review of the surgery lists floating abdominoplasty among its types and covers recovery and complications.[1]

chain: Navel is detached from the abdominal wall
Loose lower-abdominal skin and fat are removed
Navel is reattached at a natural height
Flatter, tighter midsection with a low scar
angle.text: The operation removes excess lower-abdominal skin and fat, and can tighten the underlying muscle, giving a flatter profile. The floating step is what allows the skin below the navel to be removed through a smaller incision.

infobox: Navel detached and reattached or repositioned

paras: Abdominoplasty types include complete (hip-to-hip incision, navel freed), partial or mini (smaller incision, limited skin lifting, navel may be moved lower), extended, high lateral tension and circumferential body lift.[2] In the floating variant, the navel is temporarily detached so the abdominal wall can be tightened through a smaller incision, after which the navel is reattached or repositioned.[2]
Surgeons describe variations on the navel float, including keeping the navel stalk in place in some mini-abdominoplasty techniques to avoid the navel sitting too low.

Patients commonly seek the procedure for loose skin after pregnancy or weight loss. It can be combined with liposuction, which is sometimes called a lipotuck, and with other body procedures.[2] Surgeons note the choice of a navel float can reflect a patient's wish to avoid a scar or to keep the navel's position.[3]

Typical care includes a dressing, possible compression garment and drainage of excess fluid.[2] Complications reported for abdominoplasty include seroma, hematoma, infection, delayed healing, skin or fat necrosis, scarring, sensation changes, asymmetry, blood clots and anaesthesia complications.[2] Smoking, obesity, diabetes, prior abdominal surgery and combined procedures raise risk.[2]
The Czech review notes that because of the extent of the surgical field and length of operation, systemic and local healing complications are possible.[1]

Floating abdominoplasty is a body-contouring option mentioned within the wider set of surgical procedures that people consider for torso appearance, usually in the context of excess skin rather than for fat loss alone.
Case series of umbilical float mini-abdominoplasty have been published in plastic-surgery journals. A 2024 analysis of 55,956 abdominoplasty patients compared complications by abdominoplasty type.[2]

timeline.event: Modern abdominoplasty techniques begin to develop.[2]
